groups.title: Models and Relationships
groups.question: You are modelling recipes, authors and tags in Django and need a page showing each author's number of recipes. Explain how models, relationships and aggregations work.

followUps.Defining Models and Field Types: How does a Django model map to the database?
followUps.Relationships: ForeignKey, ManyToMany: How would you model recipes with one author and many tags?
followUps.Aggregations and Annotations: Why count recipes per author with annotate instead of a Python loop?

evidence.text: Each model maps to a database table.
Each field becomes a column with a type, like text or dates.
Field options add validation and constraints, such as maximum length.
A ForeignKey creates a many-to-one link, such as many recipes to one author.
A ManyToManyField uses a join table, such as recipes and tags.
Related objects can be queried from either side of the relationship.
annotate and aggregate run counts and sums in the database with SQL.
annotate adds a computed value to each row, like a recipe count per author.
This avoids loading every row into Python, which is much faster.

groups.title: QuerySets and Database Queries
groups.question: Your recipe list filters and sorts recipes, and a teammate changed a model and the production database broke. Explain how querysets and migrations work.

followUps.QuerySet API: filter, exclude, order_by: When does a queryset actually hit the database?
followUps.Database Migrations Workflow: What do makemigrations and migrate do, and why review migrations?

evidence.text: Querysets are lazy and build up the query without running it.
filter, exclude and order_by can be chained to build the query.
The query runs only when results are needed, such as looping or converting to a list.
makemigrations writes migration files from model changes.
migrate applies them to the database.
Reviewing generated migrations catches destructive changes before they run in production.

notEnough: Only saying migrations update the database.

groups.title: PostgreSQL Integration
groups.question: You are moving from SQLite to PostgreSQL and one report needs a complex query the ORM cannot express well. Explain how you would connect and when you would use raw SQL.

followUps.Connecting Django to PostgreSQL: How do you connect Django to PostgreSQL safely?
followUps.Raw SQL and Database Functions: When would you use raw SQL or database functions, and what must you be careful of?

evidence.text: A PostgreSQL driver like psycopg is installed.
The DATABASES setting points Django to PostgreSQL.
Credentials come from environment variables, never committed code.

notEnough: Only saying you change the database setting.

evidence.text: Database functions like Coalesce or Extract push logic into SQL while staying in the ORM.
raw queries handle cases the ORM cannot express well.
Values must be passed as parameters, not formatted into the string, to avoid SQL injection.

notEnough: Only saying Django supports raw SQL.

groups.title: ORM Tooling
groups.question: You want to try a few ORM queries and understand how your models relate before writing views. Explain the tools you would use.

followUps.Django Shell for ORM Exploration: What is manage.py shell useful for?
followUps.django-extensions and Model Diagrams: What do shell_plus and graph_models add?

evidence.text: It opens a Python shell with Django set up.
You can run queries and inspect data interactively.
It helps check model behaviour before writing view code.

notEnough: Only saying it opens a shell.

evidence.text: shell_plus imports all models automatically.
graph_models generates a diagram of models and their relationships.
Both make exploring the data model faster.
